Since the solidification rates in laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) are in the range of 10³ to 10⁶ °C/s, Laves formation is expected to be minimized in AM processing as compared to castings or weldments . However, the resulting distribution, morphology and volume fraction of the Laves phase is often cited as a concern regarding its effect on the mechanical properties . The formation of discontinuous globular Laves phase along grain boundaries has been reported to improve the quasi-static room temperature strength in addition to elevated temperature stress rupture properties . Source : The JMAK (Johnson-Mehl -Avrami -Kolmogorov ) formulation is used to model diffusion-controlled transformations. Typically, a sigmoidal (or s-shaped) time evolution of the transformation starts slowly, continues relatively fast and slows down again at the end of the transformation. This function suits the typical phases formation: nucleation, growth and grain impingement.  
Réponse : Le JMAK modélise les transformations contrôlées par la diffusion. Sa forme sigmoïde est expliquée par trois étapes : la nucléation, la croissance et l'empietement des grains. [MET004:p21]
